title: Fourier Min-Entropy–Influence conjecture
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
formal: Does there exist a finite universal constant \(C>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge1\) and every Boolean function \(f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}\), some set \(S\subseteq[n]\) satisfies \(\widehat f(S)^2\ge 2^{-C I(f)}\)? Here \(I(f)\) is total influence under the uniform distribution. Equivalently, the conjecture asserts \(H_\infty(f)\le C I(f)\), with Fourier min-entropy defined below. The same constant must work for every dimension and every function.
why: Total influence measures how often individual bit changes alter an output, while Fourier min-entropy measures how weak even the strongest parity correlation can be. A universal relation would constrain all Boolean functions without representation or balance assumptions. Its distinction from full Fourier entropy matters: controlling a single coefficient asks for less than controlling the entire spectral information, yet retains a connection to fundamental influence inequalities.
status_note: The unrestricted conjecture is explicit in the 2021 primary paper and is still treated as a conjecture in the checked July 2026 Li–Tang publication. Their reported constant lower bound and Han’s general bound do not settle existence of a finite universal FMEI constant. This bounded source review does not independently verify every later proof or certify an exhaustive literature search.

progress.text: Arunachalam et al. publish their Fourier-entropy and min-entropy results. Conjecture 4.1 states the unrestricted FMEI question; Theorem 4.9 proves a bounded-read DNF case. The checked ECCC revision contains the full statements.
Biswas and Sarkar’s revised preprint gives the lower bound \(128/45\) on any universal FMEI constant; the journal publication appears in Discrete Applied Mathematics 364 (2025), pages 23–32.
Han’s paper is published online, with journal placement in Combinatorica 45 (2025), article 4. Theorem 1 bounds Fourier entropy using total influence plus a coordinate-influence entropy term.

Li and Tang’s Discrete Applied Mathematics paper reports ratios arbitrarily close to \(4\) from below and treats the unrestricted FMEI inequality as a conjecture. This is the most recent checked directly relevant source.

importance.reason: A broad structural conjecture connecting sensitivity with a guaranteed spectral coefficient for every Boolean function. It is a consequential weakening of Fourier entropy–influence with an independent connection to KKL, and recent lower bounds on its universal constant emphasize a substantial unresolved barrier rather than a single construction parameter.

sentences: The FMEI conjecture says that every Boolean function has a parity whose squared Fourier correlation is exponentially large in minus its total influence.
Both influence and Fourier coefficients use the uniform distribution on the Boolean cube.
One universal constant must cover every dimension and truth table, including constant and unbalanced functions.
The conjecture is weaker than full Fourier entropy–influence and remains meaningful because of its connection to fundamental influence inequalities.
Recent constructions force the universal constant to be at least four, while leaving the existence of any finite constant unresolved.

definitions: Write \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). For \(S\subseteq[n]\), define the parity \(\chi_S(x)=\prod_{j\in S}x_j\), with \(\chi_\varnothing(x)=1\), and the normalized Fourier coefficient \(\widehat f(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}f(x)\chi_S(x)\). Set \(p_f(S)=\widehat f(S)^2\); these nonnegative masses sum to one. Define \(H_\infty(f)=-\log_2\bigl(\max_{S\subseteq[n]}p_f(S)\bigr)\), measured in bits. The maximum is positive, so this logarithm is always defined, even if some coefficients vanish. If \(x^{\oplus j}\) is obtained by changing the sign of coordinate \(j\), define \(I_j(f)=2^{-n}|\{x\in\{-1,1\}^n:f(x)\ne f(x^{\oplus j})\}|\) and \(I(f)=\sum_{j=1}^n I_j(f)\). Equivalently \(I(f)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|S|p_f(S)\). Quantification includes constant functions, for which \(I(f)=H_\infty(f)=0\), as well as unbalanced, nonmonotone and arbitrarily complex functions. The witnessing set may be empty and may depend on the entire function. There is no algorithmic requirement to find it. In particular, the target is the largest squared Fourier coefficient, not the entropy of the truth table, the largest individual coordinate influence, or the Shannon entropy \(H(f)=\sum_{S:p_f(S)>0}p_f(S)\log_2(1/p_f(S))\). Changing the base from two to the natural exponential only rescales the universal constant.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the stated universal-constant inequality or its negation. A positive answer must establish one finite \(C>0\) for every dimension and Boolean function, with the normalized Fourier distribution and uniform influences above. A negative answer must prove that for every \(C>0\) there exist \(n\ge1\) and a nonconstant Boolean function \(f\) with \(H_\infty(f)>C I(f)\). Disproving one proposed constant, checking finitely many truth tables, or establishing a bound with a dimension-dependent factor does not settle this existence question. Determining the smallest possible constant is not required.

context_blocks.text: The named conjecture is stated explicitly as Conjecture 4.1 by Arunachalam, Chakraborty, Koucký, Saurabh and de Wolf. The draft’s saved O’Donnell book locator instead points to the Kahn–Kalai–Linial theorem and its surrounding influence theory. That book remains background provenance; the explicit research statement is anchored to the conjecture in the checked paper.

The full Fourier Entropy–Influence conjecture implies this one because \(H_\infty(f)\le H(f)\). A proof of the present target would not by itself establish the full Shannon-entropy inequality. Conversely, a refutation of this target would also refute that stronger conjecture.

The same paper verifies the conjecture for DNFs in which each variable occurs only a fixed bounded number of times. This supplies a representation-restricted result; the universal conjecture allows every Boolean truth table.

Biswas and Sarkar obtain a Boolean function with \(H_\infty(f)/I(f)=128/45\). Li and Tang’s 2026 paper reports a family with ratios tending to \(4\) from below, which forces any universal constant to be at least \(4\). These are lower bounds on a possible constant, not an unbounded sequence of ratios and hence not a refutation.

Han’s general Fourier-entropy bound contains the additional term \(\sum_j I_j(f)\log(1/I_j(f))\), with zero terms omitted. Its dependence on the separate coordinate influences does not supply the universal multiple of \(I(f)\) asked for here.
